summary: Part count, handedness, mechanisms and clearances are sound: the bolt, selector, port and mag release sit only on the gun's right as the sheet shows, the bipod folds and splays as declared, and the gates show 0 rest intersections. The craft failures are in surfacing and outline quality. The OD chassis, butt and grip read as flat extruded slabs with no visible chamfer highlight. Their traced outlines carry polyline jaggies (forend nose sawtooth, grip spur, butt-pad notches). The trigger guard is open at the bottom where the sheet draws a closed loop. The scope's black anodize reads as polished chrome (median roughness 0.29 against a table of 0.45-0.65). Wear is almost invisible, so the gun reads factory-new and CG-clean rather than 'moderate' like the sheet.

G1.note: Machined parts (rail, rings, turret saddle, bolt shroud, mag floorplate) show crisp small chamfers (close_action_right, scope_close, close_mag_well). The OD chassis, butt, riser and grip show no readable bevel at all: the side views render as flat silhouettes (right.png, close_stock_right, close_action_left), and wire_right shows no bevel loops along the chassis edges. The class widths cannot be told apart because one class barely shows.

G2.note: No continuous edge highlight on the chassis top and bottom edges, the butt perimeter, riser edges, guard or grip in any side or close view. Only q34/deployed_hero show a faint soft highlight on the forend top edge. The P-round grip and the M-chamfer chassis need edges at or above the 0.4-0.7 mm visibility minimum.

G3.note: Eyepiece rim silhouette is visibly polygonal (eyepiece_view). The trigger blade shows segment kinks (close_action_right, close_action_left). The grip outline is a stair-stepped polyline (close_stock_right, close_action_left). Barrel, scope tube and bell are smooth at review distance.

G4.note: Large chassis flats shade evenly despite long sliver triangulation (wire_right vs right.png, q34). No smoothing gradients seen on flats.

G5.note: Gates: 0 rest intersections, butt gaps min 0.0152 mm, mag seam 0.3 mm (form.json, mag.json). Visually the riser sits on its posts, rings on the rail, mag in the well. Small exception: the release-pin ring next to the paddle sits half outside the housing (close_mag_well, close_action_right). See C9.

G6.note: Hex-socket screw heads on the butt plate, receiver side and ring caps are plausible 5-7 mm heads (close_stock_right, close_action_right, scope_close). The two large flat discs on the butt are covered under C10.

G7.note: Gate families show two metal-roughness modes (anod 0.44, phos 0.70-0.80), and barrel/device phosphate reads correctly matte (close_muzzle_right). But the scope body's scope_anod median roughness of 0.292 (uv_bake_paint.json) makes it read as glossy black plastic in side views and polished chrome at grazing angles (fp_action, q34, close_scope_right). The bolt body and shroud band read mirror-chrome (close_action_right, bolt_open).

G8.note: Polymer grip and rubber pad and feet have ~0 metal fraction and read dielectric (close_stock_right, deployed_hero).

G9.note: No mirrored or stacked islands (gate: 0). Wear is so sparse (OD chip_texels 1559 on a 4K set) that its distribution cannot be read in any render. The only visible wear is a uniform bright ring on every turret and cap rim (scope_close, close_scope_right), which reads stamped-on rather than placed by cause.

G10.note: Bolt handle, ejection port, selector with F/S and mag-release paddle appear only on the right. The left views show a blank receiver and the shroud only (left.png, close_action_left). TOP shows the knob on gun-right, matching the sheet TOP crop.

G11.note: No muzzle-on render in the set. The crown chamfer, bore depth and carbon cannot be judged.

G12.note: Ejection port, forend slots and selector pocket are cut with visible walls (close_action_right, bolt_open, close_forend_right).

G13.note: No stamped sheet parts on this design. The chassis guard is a machined/cast section.

G15.note: Reads factory-new: no visible edge chips on the chassis, butt, mag or rail in any close-up (close_stock_right, close_forend_right, close_mag_well). No cavity grime in the rail slots, forend slots or port. The sheet shows moderate edge wear on the chassis corners and the forend.

G16.note: Invented or broken details: a sawtooth notch at the forend nose (C3), a thin blade-like spur under the grip toe (C4), notches on the butt-pad rear edge (C3), and random white specks on the rail and receiver flats that read as noise rather than legible rail numbers (C11). The F/S letters are allowed (user rule 2026-10-13). No text or logos otherwise.

G17.note: Whole-gun GR IoU 0.962 passes, but per-part GR fails 2/19 (form.json): trigger_guard 0.76, bolt_handle 0.35, receiver 0.46, butt 0.58, barrel 0.80. The visible consequence is the open trigger guard (C2). TOP and GL are inside the accepted conventions.

G18.note: Not judgeable from stills. game.json LOD-pop gate passes (LOD0->1 mean 0.024 px). W3 notes a late LOD2 switch from collapse LODs.

G19.note: The polymer grip shows no draft, no parting line and no rounded P-round edges. It reads as a jagged flat extrusion with stepped grooves on its side (close_stock_right, q34, deployed_hero).

G20.note: In the side views the OD reads close to the sheet's olive (gate: rendered 88,89,78 vs sheet 88,88,78). Under the 3/4 key light (deployed_hero, fp_action) it washes out to a pale grey-sage, much lighter and less saturated than the sheet Q34 at a similar angle. The polymer grip also lifts to mid-grey there.

findings.problem: Black anodize reads as polished chrome or wet plastic. There are long sharp specular streaks along the tube and bell, and in fp_action the whole tube reflects silver. Gate median roughness is 0.292, under the study's Type III anodize range of 0.45-0.65. The sheet scope is matte black.
findings.suggested_fix: Paint stage: scope_anod roughness to ~0.50 (P5-P95 0.45-0.60) with a subtle roughness micro-variation, metallic 0, base ~0.035 linear. Keep the lens at 0.05 and turret knurl flats at ~0.45. Re-check fp_action at grazing angle.

findings.problem: The guard is two hooked arms with a gap across the bottom. The design sheet panel 1 and the GR crop draw a closed rounded loop. Per-part IoU is 0.76, and the trace note says the guard bottom bar was relabelled as chassis, so the bar was apparently dropped. An open guard reads as a broken mesh at hero distance.
findings.suggested_fix: Generator: build the guard as one closed loop (bottom bar ~6-7 mm deep, same thickness as the arms, C-fillet/M-round 1 mm edges) tied to the traced loop. Re-run B3 trigger and F9 (the trigger must still clear the bar at full pull), and the trigger_guard per-part IoU.

findings.area: Traced outlines: forend nose, forend top step, mag-well underside, butt-pad rear edge, cheek-riser front
findings.problem: Outlines extruded straight from the trace keep pixel and polyline noise. There is a sawtooth notch at the forend nose (close_forend_right x~730), a bump on the forend top near the receiver, jagged facets under the mag well's front, notches on the butt pad's rear edge and a tooth on the riser underside. Real machined or moulded parts have straight lines and true arcs, so these read as broken or low-quality CG at hero distance.
findings.suggested_fix: Generator: fit the traced 2D outline to lines and arcs before extruding (e.g. Douglas-Peucker at ~0.3 mm, then snap near-collinear runs to lines and fillet corners to the class radius). Keep IoU against GR, but cap contour noise: no reversal shorter than 3 mm. Square off the forend nose as the sheet draws it.

findings.problem: The grip is a flat extrusion with a stair-stepped back and front outline, a thin blade-like spur sticking forward from the toe, and horizontal ledges on its side. The sheet grip is a rounded moulded grip with a flared base and finger contour. It shows no rounding, draft or parting line, and in side light it renders as a black cut-out.
findings.suggested_fix: Generator: loft the grip from smoothed cross-sections (rounded-rectangle/oval sections, P-round 1.5-2 mm edges, 1-2 deg draft from a centre parting plane). Delete the toe spur (or close it into the flared base the sheet shows). Smooth the outline as in C3. Paint: stipple-zone roughness 0.80 on the side panels, 0.55 on the straps, and a faint parting-line seam in the normal map.

findings.area: OD chassis, butt, cheek riser: edge treatment
findings.problem: Large aluminium chassis parts have no readable chamfer or round. Side views show flat silhouettes with no edge highlight, and the wireframe shows no bevel loops on the chassis perimeter. Machined chassis edges in the sheet catch light along every corner. This is the main reason the stock reads like a 2D cut-out.
findings.suggested_fix: Generator: bevel every chassis/butt/riser outer edge at M-chamfer 0.6-0.8 mm (rear) to 0.9 mm (forend), 1 segment at LOD0, or M-round 1.2 mm 2-3 segments on the grip-area and comb edges, with weighted normals. Bake the edge into the normal at LOD1+. Confirm with a raking-light render showing a continuous highlight (G2).

findings.problem: Wear is effectively invisible: no chips on the chassis corners, butt toe or heel, forend nose or mag floorplate, and no grime in the rail slots, forend slots or port. The sheet shows a moderately used gun. The result reads factory-clean and CG.
findings.suggested_fix: Paint stage: lift the OD edge-chip mask so 0.5-2 mm chips show on the convex edges added in C5 (target several times the current 1,559 chip texels), with a dark rim before bare aluminium. Add cavity grime (Masks B) in the rail slots, forend slot walls, port edges and screw heads. Add hand polish on the grip straps and the forend belly, and a selector arc.

findings.problem: Flutes are narrow and shallow and stop well short of the muzzle device. The sheet Q34/GR draw wide, deep, dark flutes that read clearly at 3/4 distance and run close to the device.
findings.suggested_fix: Generator: widen the flutes (~5-6 mm) and deepen them (~2 mm) with M-round ends, and match the sheet's flute count and the GR end positions. Paint: slightly darker, rougher flute floors (phos 0.80) for contrast.

findings.problem: The bolt body in the port and the shroud band read as mirror chrome, and every turret cap carries an identical bright ring. Sliding-polished steel is right in principle, but at roughness ~0.1 it reads plated. The uniform ring wear reads stamped-on.
findings.suggested_fix: Paint: bolt body roughness 0.22-0.30 with axial polish streaks; shroud band 0.30. Replace the uniform turret rim ring with intermittent edge wear limited to the cap top edge and the coin-slot ribs.

findings.problem: The pin ring beside the paddle sits on the housing edge, half in air, so it reads as a floating washer.
findings.suggested_fix: Generator: move the pin centre inside the housing face by at least one pin radius plus 1 mm, or extend a boss under it.

findings.problem: The two large round discs on the butt read as flat stickers: no bevel, knurl or recess. At ~30 mm they look larger than the small round features the sheet GR shows there.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the size against the GR crop (sheet px). Give them an M-round edge and either a recessed counterbore or a knurled rim (normal only).

findings.problem: Small white specks along the rail side and the receiver flat read as noise or z-fighting, not as rail numbers. Generic numbers are allowed, but illegible white dashes look like artefacts.
findings.suggested_fix: Paint: either render the rail numbers as legible, evenly spaced engraved numerals (darker, not white) or remove them. Keep markings recessed in the normal map with low-contrast fill.

findings.area: OD colour under the 3/4 key light
findings.problem: Side views match the sheet's olive, but in the 3/4 shots the OD goes pale grey-sage and the polymer grip goes mid-grey. The sheet Q34 at a similar angle stays clearly olive and dark.
findings.suggested_fix: Paint: lower OD roughness slightly (0.62 -> ~0.55) and nudge saturation up so the hue holds under strong key light. Polymer base to ~0.025 linear. Re-run the G20 crop match on the Q34 angle as well as GR.

findings.area: Scope eyepiece rim and trigger blade faceting
findings.problem: The eyepiece's outer rim silhouette is visibly polygonal in the eyepiece view (the player's closest view of the attachment), and the trigger blade shows segment kinks.
findings.suggested_fix: Generator: raise the eyepiece and objective rim segments to 64+ (or keep 48 with analytic custom normals plus a rim bevel). Sweep the trigger blade curve at 7.5 deg or less per segment.
